source_text: sicut fames et sitis et digestio, non voluntatis imperium, sed consensum requirunt Cum ventum fuerit ut filii seminentur, ad voluntatis prorsus nutum membra in hoc opus creata famulari; et nisi eorum impedimenta, aut de infirmitate, aut de immoderatione proveniant, servire animi imperio hoc genus motus in his habendum putasti, quae multa in nostro corpore ordine suo ac dispensatione secreta, voluntatis non imperium, sed consensum requirunt
pass_a_gloss: As fames and may-be and digestio, not of-will imperium, but consensum requirunt when/with ventum fuerit so-that/as sons seminentur, to of-will altogether nutum members in this work creata famulari; and unless their impedimenta, or about/from infirmitate, or about/from immoderatione proveniant, servire animi imperio this genus movement in these habendum putasti, which many-things in nostro in-the-body ordine his-own and dispensatione secreta, of-will not imperium, but consensum requirunt.

lemmas.lexica: LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will

pass_b_english: When it comes to sowing children, the members created for this work serve precisely at the will’s direction. Unless impediments arise from weakness or excess, they obey the mind’s command.
This kind of movement belongs among the many things in our body that, through their own order and hidden arrangement, require the will’s consent, not its command.
Like hunger, thirst, and digestion, they require the will’s consent, not its command.
I feel ashamed and am prevented by horror from speaking about such things, but compelled by necessity.

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Image of God in the soul; keep soul not 'mind' or 'life-force'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
